To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heat transfer performance of R114/R12 condensing mixtures was depressed below that of the pure refrigerants and that the performance depression increased with increasing R12 concentration.

the heat transfer performance of condensing mixtures of R114 and R12 was depressed by up to 55%, and the performance depression was attributed to a transport resistance that was enhanced by the presence of a more volatile component (in this case R12).

the heat transfer performance of non-azeotropic R114/R12 refrigerant mixtures in horizontal condensing is substantially depressed below that of the pure refrigerants and that this depression is due to an added transport resistance. 1 fig., 2 tabs., 1 ref. In summary, our research is concerned with
the condensation of refrigerants on horizontal finned-tube condensers.
the development of a new type of refrigeration heat transfer device, the finned tube condenser.
the heat transfer characteristics of R-12, R-114 and their mixtures in the horizontal orientation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mixtures of R12/R114 are not recommended for use in heat pumps, and the results obtained in this study provide the rationale for this recommendation.
R114 and R12 mixtures are not recommended for use in condensers operating in the condensing mode. 2 refs., 6 figs.
R12/R114 mixtures are not recommended for use as condensing refrigerants in heat pumps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the case of condensation, R12 is a poor choice as an addition to R114.
the condensing heat transfer performance of mixtures of R12 and R114 is significantly lower than for the pure components.
the condensing performance of mixtures of R114 and R12 on horizontal finned-tube condensers is significantly lower than the single-component performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, condensing heat transfer performance is not improved by using azeotropic mixtures of refrigerants.
condensation performance is very sensitive to mixture composition, with the most volatile component being preferentially transported to the condensate side.

condensing heat transfer of refrigerant mixtures on horizontal external finned tubes is significantly lower than that of pure refrigerants, and the effect increases with the concentration of the more volatile refrigerant in the mixtures.
